items.title: Welcome to Mr.EA
items.text:
Mr.EA is a web site containing reflections, maybe an occassional cautionary tale, and some adviocacy from the authors. It is based upon many years of trans-Atlantic conversations arising from practical and real issues arising from the authors' own experiences in their daily work as Enterprise Architects across many industries.

The authors freely admit that the topics covered are not backed by formal research, which is why the site contents are split into two main streams:

  • Reflections - in which the authors have experienced some form of challenge or a question arising for which there has been no answer recroded within the searching they have subsequently done. These pieces thus, whilst unsupported by any academic practice or research, are written to provide some views of what went through the authors minds
  • Thoughts - in which the authors, in the absence of any formal disciurse, aim to apply some thinking about what might happen, or what might be useful

In all of these pieces, and across the site in general, it is our hope that these arcticles provide some insight and value to anyone entering, or practicing, what is called Entrepirse Architecture or EA. Given the authors names are Murali and Russell, hopefully the site name becomes clear

items.title: Russell
items.text:
Enterprise Architect based in Yorkshire, England

Russell has spent over 45 years in the computing and technology working in Supply-Chain, Telecoms, and more recently in public sector across Agriculture and Policing. Currently Russell is engaged as an Enterprise Architect working on applied science delivery in a large UK Government agency.

Academically, Russell started as a Computer Scientist, and it has been through developing a career alongside the seismic change brought about by microprocessors. These changes have influenced much of the insight that Russell uses as an Enterprise Architect having experienced the development of the role and approaches as business and organisationla needs have changed.

items.title: Architecting in the organisational culture
items.text:
Does Organisational Culture Impact the delivery of Architecture

We can complete our training in architecture, and pass our certifications. But on going back to our organisations and producing architrectural artafects as we learned, do they have any real impact as part of devlivring our value as archietcts?

items.title: Frameworks vs Examples
items.text:
How Effectieve is is setting Archicturral Frameworks

Most architectural approaches advocate the setting or Architectue Frameworks to direct and giovern the delivery of architecture. Given the potential gap between examples given at training, and the real needs of any organisation, is there a better way to establish architectural standards?
